summary: This EOB (which is not a bill) explains your knee MRI on May 14, 2026 at Lakeside Imaging Center. Your plan approved $850 for the scan. Because you had not yet met your yearly deductible, the full $850 approved amount went toward your deductible. The extra $950 your provider billed above the approved price is written off — you never owe that part.

lines.explanation: You owe $850 for this MRI. That is the plan's full allowed (approved) amount, and it was applied to your deductible — the amount you pay each year before the plan starts sharing costs. PR-1 (deductible) confirms this, and the good news is it 'counts toward both your deductible and your out-of-pocket maximum.' The $950 gap between the $1,800 billed charge and the $850 approved price is CO-45 (the discount your provider agreed to). That difference is written off by the provider — you do not owe it because this was in-network care.

citations.quote: PR-1 means this amount was applied to your deductible, the amount you pay each year before the plan starts sharing costs.
It counts toward both your deductible and your out-of-pocket maximum.
The difference is written off by the provider. Members do not owe CO-45 amounts for in-network care.

actions: When a bill arrives from Lakeside Imaging Center, verify it says $850 — not $1,800. The $950 difference is the provider's write-off, not your charge.
Keep this EOB with your records. The $850 counts toward your deductible and your out-of-pocket maximum, which lowers what you pay later this year.
If the provider's bill shows any amount other than $850, call their billing office and ask them to match it to this EOB before you pay anything.
